title: Zong massacre
summary: From 29 November 1781 the crew of the slave ship Zong threw enslaved Africans into the sea over several days on its voyage from Ghana to Jamaica: 122 were thrown overboard and 10 more jumped, 132 deaths among 442 aboard. The owners claimed insurance for the loss, and a 1783 King's Bench case, not a murder trial, followed.

uncertainty.note: The killings began 29 November and ran into early December 1781 (insurance.museum); the National Maritime Museum and Master Mariners give 132 deaths, while insurance.museum counts 122 thrown overboard plus 10 who jumped. The ship reached Jamaica on 22 December 1781. The position at sea was not given.

importance.justification: The mass killing and the insurance case that followed became a defining episode in the history of the Atlantic slave trade and its legal and moral reckoning.

audience_note: Describes the mass killing of enslaved people by drowning. Casualty figures vary by source (132 deaths in most accounts).

related.because: The Zong was a slave ship carrying captives across the Atlantic.

beats.caption: In mid-August 1781 the Zong left Ghana for Jamaica with 442 enslaved people aboard.
From 29 November the crew threw enslaved people overboard over several days; 132 died in all.
The owners' insurance claim reached the Court of King's Bench, handled as a property dispute, not a murder prosecution.
